svg.title: Why keepdims=True matters: a silent wrong answer against a correct one
svg.desc: Two hand-drawn panels subtracting the per-row maximum from a three-by-three array. The left panel, in alert red and labelled without keepdims, calls np.max with axis one; the maximum comes back as three, six, nine of shape three, a one-dimensional array that is padded to one by three and stretches downward. Its result is shown in full: minus two, minus four, minus six on the first row, one, minus one, minus three on the second, four, two, nought on the third, and it is labelled silently wrong because three is taken off column nought of every row rather than off row nought. The right panel, in success green and labelled with keepdims equals True, gets a column of shape three by one, which stretches across the columns, and every row of its result ends at zero. A band advises always passing keepdims when reducing along an axis and then operating against the original array, since it costs nothing and the failure it prevents raises no error.
svg.text: One keyword between a right answer and a wrong one
Subtracting the per-row maximum. Both calls run, both return a 3-by-3, and only one is correct.
3 comes off column 0 of every row, not off row 0.
No error is raised, and the result even has the right shape.
3 is taken off row 0, 6 off row 1, 9 off row 2.
Every row now ends at zero, which is what softmax needs.
When reducing along an axis and then operating against the original 2-D array, always pass keepdims=True.
It costs nothing when it is not needed, and the failure it prevents raises no error.
